findings.claim: Q1's key and Q5's key share the authored 4-gram "the results so far", a phrase that occurs in no distractor anywhere in the unit and nowhere in the passage. Two of the five keys therefore carry a private lexical fingerprint the wrong answers do not, and the integrated cross-question sweep records no disposition of it.
findings.evidence: Q1/C (key) = "How phages are matched to particular infections, and how far the results so far reach." Q5/B (key) = "Interested, but unwilling to let the results so far settle the question." Programmatic check on the shipped file: the 4-gram "the results so far" appears in exactly those two option strings; `passage.lower().count('results so far')` = 0 (the passage's only nearby wording is Bellinghast's quoted "Our results suggest that phages add something in a subset of these infections"); and no non-key option in any of the five questions contains it. Calibration over all 71 shipped multi-question units in batches/*/candidates-final: only 2 units show ANY cross-key 4-gram that is absent from both the passage and every distractor — this one and elf-b7-001 ("that faster repair genuinely" / "faster repair genuinely helps" / "repair genuinely helps but", also Q1&Q5).
findings.why: Integrated review's cross-question row is exactly where a key-to-key echo has to be caught: it is invisible to G-STEM (which judges one item blind at a time), invisible to G-KEY (which judges one item against the passage), and invisible to M-TELL (which measures option length, not shared lexis — I re-ran mech's own tokenizer and confirm the key is the strict-longest option in 0/5, so the metadata's M-TELL claim is true and is not the issue). Severity is minor, not major, because the shared string is an evaluative hedge frame rather than the answer content, exploiting it requires having already solved Q1, and elf-b7-001 establishes that the corpus has shipped the same shape before. It is a real unrecorded property of the unit, consistent with the recorded MINOR_NOTES rather than a refutation of it.

findings.claim: Q5's WHY-DISTRACTORS defends the key against option C with a factual claim about the passage that the passage contradicts: it says Quilvey's readier position is "offered in her own voice", but Quilvey has no direct speech anywhere in the text. Her whole position reaches the reader through the writer's own indirect narration — which, if anything, is the weakest form of authorial distancing and is the one place a complaining C-picker has a foothold.
findings.evidence: Q5 rationale: "C = role_or_attribution_swap – Quilvey's readiness to use a matched phage as a standard option is her position, offered in her own voice and immediately fenced by her own limit; the writer reports it without joining it." A scan of every quotation-mark span in the shipped passage returns exactly two, both Bellinghast: "Our results suggest that phages add something in a subset of these infections," and "They cannot tell us how large that something is." Everything attributed to Quilvey is the writer's sentence: "Josephine Quilvey, who treats bone and joint infection at one of the four hospitals, is readier than that. She would offer a matched phage as a standard option in infected joint replacements … and she is deliberate about the limit: she means that setting, not resistant infection at large." The same misreading is already on the gate record: G-DISTRACTOR's q:5 flag note asserts the piece "does quote both a cautious researcher … and a readier clinician (“Josephine Quilvey … is readier than that”)" — the string it puts in quotation marks as the clinician's is in fact the writer's own evaluative narration, so two independent records now rest on a quotation that does not exist.
findings.why: Rationale factual accuracy is the pedagogy stage's own probe, and this is a checkable false statement about the text inside the teaching payload for the unit's hardest item. It does not flip the key: C is still defeated decisively by three writer-owned judgments the rationale also cites and that I verified verbatim — "which is worth saying before any of the numbers that follow", "the care is warranted: without a comparison group, a recovery in a patient taking four drugs says little about the fifth", and "that trial, not any series, will decide whether the treatment becomes ordinary" — all of which are flatly incompatible with C's "should already be a standard option". So the recorded MINOR_FIXES verdict stands; the fix is to replace "offered in her own voice" with the accurate "attributed to her and fenced by her own limit", which is stronger anyway because it survives the student who notices the quotation asymmetry.

findings.claim: Q3's WHY-DISTRACTORS makes a false locational claim about the passage: it tells the student the refutation of option D sits "in the next sentence", when the quoted phrase is four sentences further on and separated from the referenced material by a two-sentence direct quotation.
findings.evidence: Q3 rationale: "D = outside_knowledge about method – it supplies the controlled comparison a reader expects a published series to contain, while the passage says the opposite in the next sentence (\"without a comparison group\")." Paragraph 3 sentence order in the shipped passage: S1 "The clinical record is thin, and honest about being thin." / S2 "A series published last year followed sixty-three patients … eleven had the implant taken out anyway." / S3 "Every patient in it was also on antibiotics … the hospitals had referred the cases they judged most likely to respond." / S4 “Our results suggest that phages add something in a subset of these infections,” Bellinghast says. / S5 “They cannot tell us how large that something is.” / S6 "She is careful about what the series will bear, and the care is warranted: without a comparison group, a recovery in a patient taking four drugs says little about the fifth." The rationale's immediately preceding clause (its rebuttal of C) quotes S3, so "the next sentence" resolves to S4 under the only available antecedent; the target phrase is in S6.
findings.why: Integrated review's contract is that a rationale's pointers into the text resolve. The quoted span itself is verbatim (I re-ran a programmatic re-quote check: all 18 quoted spans across the five rationales appear verbatim in the current passage or current option text, one differing only in the sentence-initial capital of "The other twenty-five"), so a student following the quote still lands correctly — but a student following the pointer looks in the wrong place. Cosmetic, one-word fix ("later in the paragraph"), and exactly the class the recorded MINOR_NOTES verdict already covers.
